tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing scenarios (call fails with access/validation errors, nobody can see what the model is doing, is Bedrock set up correctly), explicitly lists trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention logging, IAM, service control policies or marketplace subscriptions by name'), and remains concise at a few sentences.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Bedrock call fails with an access, validation or throttling error, when nobody can see what the model is doing, or when someone asks whether Bedrock is set up correctly, even if they do not mention logging, IAM, service control policies or marketplace subscriptions by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining generic AWS/Bedrock concepts and goes straight into domain-specific procedures, check-ids, and non-obvious API behaviors (e.g., empty logging config meaning disabled). Tables and router are dense but information-dense rather than padded with generic explanations.
tests.evidence: An empty response with no `loggingConfig` means logging is DISABLED, which is LLM-INV-001 (CRITICAL), not a healthy or indeterminate state

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (full check catalog with severities, citations, remediation specifics) lives in references/checks-model-invocation.md; the body only has a summary table of check-ids/severities/short descriptions, which is reasonable overview content, not the detailed material itself.
tests.evidence: Full detection rules, remediations, and citations: `references/checks-model-invocation.md`.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All four reference files are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.
tests.evidence: `references/collection-reference.md` (Model invocation and Access control sections). CloudWatch metric names and the invocation-log error-pattern table are in `references/metrics-and-logs.md`.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References specify precise triggering conditions for loading each file, e.g. the router table ties each reference to a specific operator question/condition.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (IAM deny vs SCP deny distinction, logging empty-response interpretation) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while flexible areas (how to review invocation patterns) are described with purpose rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: An SCP deny overrides every account-level IAM allow... do NOT prescribe an IAM fix. Escalate to the org admin with the specific SCP policy name and deny statement

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where choices exist (e.g., streaming vs buffered, Converse vs native API), the skill frames them as diagnostic checks against best practice rather than listing many equal tool options; no menu of equal arbitrary alternatives is presented.
tests.evidence: Should i stream or use Converse, should this move to batch | Invocation pattern against streaming, Converse and batch adoption

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure teaches a generalizable method (confirm scope, read logging config, enumerate models, review IAM, diagnose access, review patterns, assemble findings) applicable to any Bedrock account, not a one-off instance task.
tests.evidence: Run the LLM-INV family against the account under review in the target region. Work the steps in order and track progress against this checklist.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus Error Handling section documenting non-obvious API quirks and misconceptions.
tests.evidence: "GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration came back empty, so logging is in some neutral or unknown state." An empty response with no loggingConfig means logging is DISABLED
